t: For an additional amount for “International information and educational activities”, $11,500,000; and the limitation under this head in the Department of State Appropriation Act, 1950, on the amount available for transfer to other appropriations of the Department of State is increased by $90,000: Provided, That funds appropriated under this head shall be available for retroactive salary increases for the fiscal year 1949, as authorized by the Act of July 6, 1949 (Public Law 160), to the extent that appropriations for said fiscal year are insufficient therefore: Provided further, That $10,475,000 of this appropriation shall be available until expended, without regard to section 3709 of the Revised Statutes, exclusively for the purchase, construction, and improvement of buildings and facilities, purchase and installation of necessary equipment for radio transmission and reception, and the acquisition of land and interest in land by purchase, lease, rental, or otherwise: Provided further, That land may be acquired outside the continental United States without regard to section 355 of the Revised Statutes, and title to any land so acquired shall be approved by the Secretary of State.

fable.w: This is an appropriations provision that funds international information activities, radio facilities, land acquisition and retroactive salary increases. The only procedural step that could be mistaken for participation is approval of land title by the Secretary of State, a federal official inside the government. Nothing requires consultation, hearings, comment, rulemaking, an advisory body, or a right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: title to any land so acquired shall be approved by the Secretary of State

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard appropriations provision that authorizes funding for specific activities and sets conditions on how those funds can be used (e.g., for retroactive salary increases or building construction). It does not require consultation, coordination, or participation with any non-federal entities, such as the public, states, or private organizations. The only actors mentioned are federal officials (Secretary of State) and the government itself.
qwen_block.s: For an additional amount for “International information and educational activities”, $11,500,000; and the limitation under this head in the Department of State Appropriation Act, 1950, on the amount available for transfer to other appropriations of the Department of State is increased by $90,000

opus.w: This is an appropriations provision that sets funding amounts, transfer limits and allowed uses. The only decision-maker it names is the Secretary of State, a federal official, approving land titles. Waiving the competitive-bidding rule (section 3709) and allowing land purchases or leases are procurement matters, not outside participation in a federal decision. No state, expert, company or member of the public is consulted or given a way to object.
opus.s: title to any land so acquired shall be approved by the Secretary of State.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The section mentions waiving section 3709 of the Revised Statutes (the rule requiring advertised competitive bidding), acquiring land "by purchase, lease, rental," and having the Secretary of State approve land titles. That could look like outside parties being involved in federal decisions. It isn't. Bidding and procurement work like applying for contracts, and here the bidding rule is waived anyway. Approving land titles is done only by the Secretary of State, who is inside the federal government. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation or right to sue appears anywhere.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriations provision that authorizes funding for international information activities and the acquisition of land and facilities. It specifies that the Secretary of State must approve title to land acquired outside the continental United States, but this is an internal administrative check, not a participation mechanism involving outside parties. There is no requirement for public comment, consultation with non-federal entities, or involvement of an advisory board with outside members.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "title to any land so acquired shall be approved by the Secretary of State" implies a process where outside parties (land sellers) participate. However, this is a standard administrative approval of a transaction, not a consultation or coordination with outside parties *before* a policy decision is made. The section is purely an appropriations bill detailing funding limits and conditions for spending. There is no mention of public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, consultation with states/tribes, or rights to sue. All actors mentioned (Secretary of State, Department of State) are inside the federal government.
